requirement: A lessee must submit the results of its site characterization surveys to BOEM with its Site Assessment Plan (SAP), Construction and Operations Plan (COP), or General Activities Plan (GAP).
scope: Atlantic Outer Continental Shelf, site characterization surveys, all phases
related_domains: environmental impact assessment; marine biology; regulatory compliance

requirement: The information will be used by BOEM, other Federal agencies, and potentially affected states in the preparation of National Environmental Policy Act (NEPA) documents.
scope: Atlantic Outer Continental Shelf, NEPA documentation

requirement: A plan (SAP, COP, or GAP) must describe biological, social, and economic resource information potentially affected by activities proposed in the SAP, COP, or GAP.
scope: All offshore wind farm projects
related_domains: environmental impact assessment; biological resources; social impact; economic resources

requirement: Activities proposed in the plan will be conducted in a manner that does not cause undue harm or damage to natural resources, wildlife, property, the marine, coastal, or human environment.
scope: All phases of offshore wind farm projects
related_domains: environmental protection; wildlife conservation; marine environment

requirement: Applicants must submit with SAPs and COPs proposed measures for avoiding, minimizing, reducing, eliminating, and monitoring environmental impacts.
scope: SAPs and COPs for offshore wind farm projects
related_domains: environmental impact assessment; monitoring; mitigation measures

requirement: The lessee should include in their survey plan a description of the mitigation measures that will be followed to avoid or minimize adverse effects, including any potential incidental take, and environmental impacts to critical habitat as designated under the ESA.
scope: Survey activity on the lease area.
related_domains: environmental impact assessment; habitat protection; wildlife conservation

requirement: BOEM may determine that it is prudent for a developer to resurvey some or all of the lease area in the event survey results are insufficient.
scope: Survey activity on the lease area.

requirement: BOEM may require a lessee to conduct post-construction surveys to assess impacts of operations on a species as a condition of SAP or COP approval.
scope: Post-construction phase for marine mammal and sea turtle impacts.

requirement: The marine mammal and sea turtle survey plan should include a description of the geographic area to be surveyed, issues to be investigated, hypotheses, assumptions, data collection techniques, standards, résumés of Protected Species Observers (PSOs), analytical and statistical techniques, and measures to ensure quality control.
scope: Survey plan for marine mammals and sea turtles.
related_domains: data collection; marine biology; environmental monitoring

requirement: Permits may be required by the NMFS and/or USFWS for certain aerial and vessel-based surveys.
scope: Marine mammal and sea turtle surveys
source: Marine Mammal Protection Act Incidental Harassment Authorization (50 CFR Part 216 Subpart I)
related_domains: environmental impact assessment; marine mammal protection; sea turtle conservation

requirement: BOEM recommends that an applicant submit a marine mammal and sea turtle survey plan at least 90 days in advance of the survey taking place.
scope: Marine mammal and sea turtle surveys
related_domains: survey planning; marine mammal protection; sea turtle conservation

requirement: Obtain all necessary permits prior to conducting surveys (e.g., MMPA and ESA scientific research permits).
scope: Surveys for marine mammals and sea turtles.
related_domains: environmental impact assessment; marine biology; permitting

requirement: Design line-transect surveys to ensure that the data obtained are of sufficient quality so as to facilitate detection of marine mammals and sea turtles and to minimize bias associated with abundance and density estimates.
scope: Surveys for marine mammals and sea turtles.
source: Buckland et al., 2001; 2008; Roberts et al. 2016
related_domains: data quality; marine biology; statistical analysis

requirement: Surveys should start after sunrise when there is enough light to identify protected species.
scope: Surveys for marine mammals and sea turtles.

requirement: Use at least two qualified, experienced, NMFS-approved PSOs with reticle binoculars, to identify marine mammal and sea turtle species.
scope: Surveys for marine mammals and sea turtles.

requirement: Record weather conditions at the start of each transect line (i.e., Beaufort Sea State, wind direction, visibility, % cloud cover, glare, temperature) as well as the time of day and names of observers.
scope: Survey phase

requirement: Record the time of each marine mammal and sea turtle sighting, record the GPS position of each observation along transect line, record the number of marine mammals and sea turtles seen and record their behavior (resting, foraging, traveling, evading, etc.).
scope: Survey phase

requirement: Estimate the actual distance and bearing for all detections so that Distance Sampling techniques can be used to correct for species missed at greater distances from the ship.
scope: Survey phase

requirement: Before each survey, surveyors should calibrate distance estimation using a laser rangefinder on objects (e.g., buoys) at a variety of distances.
scope: Survey phase

requirement: Note any injured or dead protected species and immediately report these to BOEM and regional NMFS stranding hotline and record all details surrounding these events.
scope: Survey phase

requirement: Completion of any necessary permit requirements (e.g., Marine Mammal Protection Act and Endangered Species Act scientific research permits).
scope: Survey phase
related_domains: environmental impact assessment; marine mammal protection; species conservation

requirement: Surveys should be flown at an altitude of 305 meters (m) at a speed of 185 km/h.
scope: Survey execution

requirement: Weather conditions before take-off and at start of survey should be: sea state < Beaufort 4, absence of rain or fog, visibility > 3 km.
scope: Survey execution

requirement: Transects should be orientated perpendicular to the coast and spaced approximately 3 kilometers (km) apart.
scope: Survey methodology

requirement: Provide geo-referenced, species-specific/taxonomic group digital maps and density estimates, associated variance (95% confidence Intervals), as well as raw sighting and effort data.
scope: Data presentation phase
related_domains: environmental impact assessment; marine biology; data reporting

requirement: Account for detectability. To estimate the density and abundance for each species viewed on the water, use distance data collected from line transect sampling to model a distance function.
scope: Data analysis phase

requirement: Analyses should use recent versions of Distance software which allows covariates (observer, sea state, etc.) to be incorporated into the estimation of detection functions.
scope: Data analysis phase

requirement: Hydrophones must be able to record a large bandwidth or several band widths (using multiple receivers) and should be calibrated to sample at various times of the day and night and at different frequency ranges to ensure sampling of various sound sources and vocalizations from large whales and small cetaceans.
scope: Project area

requirement: The number of hydrophones necessary will be dependent on the size of the project area, with a minimum of two hydrophones placed approximately six (6) miles apart.
scope: Project area

requirement: Reports must include identification of all vocalizing species, if possible, but especially species of interest; descriptions of monthly and/or seasonal presence of all species; any trends in vocalization patterns; spatial presence of species; ambient noise analysis.
scope: Passive-acoustic monitoring data reporting phase.
related_domains: environmental impact assessment; marine biology; acoustic monitoring

requirement: BOEM recommends that PAM data be provided to the National Oceanographic Data Center or other appropriate Federal data archive.
scope: Data archiving for passive-acoustic monitoring.

requirement: BOEM strongly recommends the lessee provide quarterly and annual progress reports to assist BOEM in tracking the progress and implementation of surveys, and to evaluate the quality of environmental information collected.
scope: Environmental monitoring and reporting for offshore wind farm surveys
related_domains: environmental impact assessment; marine mammal protection; sea turtle conservation

scope: Marine mammal and sea turtle survey results for offshore wind farms
related_domains: environmental impact assessment; marine mammal protection; sea turtle conservation

requirement: These progress reports should highlight survey findings and include (at a minimum): number of surveys conducted, dates, start and end times, weather conditions.
scope: Reporting requirements for marine mammal and sea turtle surveys
related_domains: environmental monitoring; marine mammal protection; sea turtle conservation

requirement: BOEM recommends that all data be processed, validated, and made available as needed to BOEM.
scope: Data management for survey efforts related to offshore wind farms.

scope: Regulatory framework for offshore renewable energy development.
